payload.reason: One proposal (practice), and every piece of it has already been measured on b719e31: the attribute Theory, the admin-share assertions and the SMB-LOOPBACK assertion. The slice changes only test code, and Scanner.cs stays byte-identical. The one check no stage has run yet is the acceptance repro's regex reader against the edited tree. Build runs it as case 14.
payload.selection_rationale:
The practice proposal is selected whole. It fits what the survey measured is already there.
- Both gates in Scanner.cs work: the probe read 3/3 asked locally and 0/0 on the shares. Only the assertions are missing. Mutants A and B each keep the suite at 870/870.
- LastAccessAsked and LastAccessKept are internal but visible to tests (ScanResult.cs:188, :211; csproj:10).
- TempTree.AddAttributes sets 0x1000, 0x80000 and 0x100000 on a folder as an ordinary user.
- The default suite already scans \\localhost\C$ and \\127.0.0.1\C$ in ContainerLayerStoreTests.cs:778-814 and asserts nothing about last access.

Every component was spiked:
- The Theory: 3/3 rows pass unmutated. Mutant A fails all 3. Each single-bit drop fails only its own row.
- The admin-share asserts: they pass unmutated under both TEMPs and fail under B (asked 5, kept 5).
- Both together: 873/873 unmutated. A fails exactly the 3 rows. B fails exactly the admin-share Fact.
- The SMB-LOOPBACK asserts: asked 0 unmutated and 3 under B, but only under a real user logon.

The proposal raised over_engineering_flag against a Stryker runner, an injectable remote-detection seam, and a second share fixture or rig. That warning is taken. Nothing is added beyond nine assertion lines and one three-row Theory.

There are two deliberate departures from the slice text:
1. A three-row Theory replaces the single Offline Fact the slice names. It is a superset: the Offline row is exactly that Fact. The spike showed the extra rows each catch a bit dropped from the mask, which an Offline-only Fact would miss.
2. The remote-gate kill also goes into the default-suite admin-share Fact. The spike's constraint says the SMB-LOOPBACK test is opt-in and cannot run as SYSTEM (error 1312), so on its own it gives no standing protection. The survey marked criterion (b) checked_by: person.

OverrideQueryError is rejected: its call numbering is unchecked, and it would rewrite the size probe's queries too.

components.name: Cloud-attribute Theory (attribute gate)
components.responsibility:
Pins the `(attributes & CloudFolderAttributes) != 0` clause of Scanner.KeepsLastAccess (Scanner.cs:298), one row per bit a user can set. Rows are [InlineData(FileAttributes.Offline)], [InlineData((FileAttributes)0x80000)] // PINNED and [InlineData((FileAttributes)0x100000)] // UNPINNED. They are literals, never derived from Scanner.CloudFolderAttributes.

Tree: a\one.txt (1 B), off\one.txt (1 B), off\inner\two.txt (2 B), then tree.AddAttributes(off, attribute).

Assertions, in this order:
1. Precondition: Scans.Listing(root)["off"].Attributes & attribute == attribute. If NTFS drops the bit, the row goes red instead of passing vacuously.
2. Status == Completed.
3. Totals.Bytes == 4.
4. LastAccessAsked == 3 (root, a, off\inner).

Kept is not asserted. Suggested name: AFolderWithACloudAttributeIsNotAskedToKeepItsLastAccessTimeButIsStillEntered. It sits beside NothingUnderASyncRootIsAskedToKeepItsLastAccessTime (:96-110), which covers the third gate. No Trait, no Skip, and no Path.GetTempPath (#423).
components.key_interactions:

- TempTree: root under %TEMP%\fsa-tests\<guid>, redirected to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when TEMP is under the Windows folder.
- TempTree.AddAttributes (TempTree.cs:233-234).

- The internal ScanResult.LastAccessAsked, through InternalsVisibleTo.

Measured by the spike: 3/3 green under both TEMPs, 3/3 red under mutant A, each single-bit mutant red only on its own row, and 0 leftover folders over 10 runs.

contracts.name: Default suite green unmutated, red under each named mutant
contracts.notes:
Command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --logger trx

Run it under TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, through a wrapper script that sets both variables in the child process, not `pwsh -Command "$env:TEMP=..."` (#371, #392).

Expected:
- Unmutated: 873/873.
- Mutant A (Scanner.cs:298 `if (!_keepLastAccess || (attributes & CloudFolderAttributes) != 0)` becomes `if (!_keepLastAccess)`): exactly the 3 Theory rows fail.
- Mutant B (Scanner.cs:286 `remote = io.Query(...) == 0;` becomes `_ = io.Query(...); remote = false;`): exactly the admin-share Fact fails.

Rules for mutant runs:
- Only in a `git archive HEAD` scratch copy, with absolute paths.
- Each edit must match exactly once.
- Build with --no-incremental, and confirm the test-bin FsAnalyser.Core.dll was written after the edit.
- Afterwards `git -C <worktree> diff --exit-code src` must return 0. The survey stage once wrote a mutant into the worktree through a relative path.
contracts.error_cases: A mutant run that executes fewer tests than the unmutated run under the same TEMP is void. A failure outside the expected set is re-run under both TEMPs before anyone calls it a regression.

key_decisions.decision: No product code changes. Scanner.cs, SynchronousIoCancel.cs, ScanResult.cs and Kernel32.cs stay byte-identical.
key_decisions.rationale: The investigation and the survey both measured that both gates work: the probe read 3/3 locally and 0/0 on the shares. The cause is missing assertions, not a scanner fault.

key_decisions.decision: Default-suite protection for the remote gate goes into the existing admin-share Fact in ContainerLayerStoreTests. No new share Fact and no new seam.
key_decisions.rationale: It is the only placement measured to kill mutant B on every default run on this PC (asked 5 vs 0, both TEMPs). The SMB-LOOPBACK test is opt-in and cannot run as SYSTEM, so on its own it gives no standing protection.

key_decisions.decision: Do not use SynchronousIoCancel.OverrideQueryError to fake remote=true on local NTFS.
key_decisions.rationale: Its call numbering was never checked. It rewrites the error of every Query, so it could also hit the size probe's queries. The admin-share route is measured; this one is not.

key_decisions.decision: Use a three-row Theory (Offline, Pinned, Unpinned) instead of the single Offline Fact the slice text names.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike showed each single-bit drop from CloudFolderAttributes fails only its own row. An Offline-only Fact would let a Pinned or Unpinned bit drop out of the mask unseen. The Offline row is exactly the Fact the slice asks for.

key_decisions.decision: Theory rows are literal attribute values, never derived from Scanner.CloudFolderAttributes.
key_decisions.rationale: Rows derived from the mask under test would vanish along with a dropped bit, and the test would agree with whatever the code says.

key_decisions.decision: The Theory asserts Asked == 3 and Bytes == 4 exactly, with a listing precondition per row. It does not assert Kept.
key_decisions.rationale: These are the values measured under both TEMPs. Kept depends on the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES open succeeding, which ties it to Controlled Folder Access (Q-101, #424). That dependency is not needed to kill mutant A.

key_decisions.decision: The share scans assert both Asked == 0 and Kept == 0.
key_decisions.rationale: Kept is what pins the actual SetFileInformationByHandle on the server: under B it was 4 of 4 kept. Asking for both costs one line and states the hazard directly.

key_decisions.decision: Keep the admin-share Fact's `continue` when Directory.Exists(share) is false. Add no host-count assertion.
key_decisions.rationale: Turning the skip into a failure would change the semantics of SL-095's Fact on PCs without admin shares, which is outside this slice. The vacuity risk is recorded as a case and filed instead.

key_decisions.decision: Proving that the SMB-LOOPBACK assertion bites is a person's check, filed at design time. It is not a build or validate gate.
key_decisions.rationale: The survey marked criterion (b) checked_by: person. New-SmbMapping changes this machine's SMB mappings, the project files that pass as a person's run (SL-039, SL-059), and SYSTEM gets error 1312. An obligation re-routed to a person during build halts validate (#420).

key_decisions.decision: No KnownWorkarounds entry and no setting.
key_decisions.rationale: This slice works around no outside defect. It adds assertions to existing M6 behaviour. Not writing last access over SMB is a design rule from SL-056, not a workaround for a broken component. A share reporting the server volume's 'NTFS' is documented redirector behaviour.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken whole: the three-row Theory, the admin-share asserts, the SMB-LOOPBACK asserts filed as a person's check, and the repro left unedited. Its over_engineering_flag is honoured. Every component was spiked on b719e31 before this design.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing here has survived a disagreement yet, and the reviewer downstream is the first to argue with it.

**Checked against reality instead.**
1. The attribute gate can hide the remote gate. If a share tree carried cloud bits, mutant B would read 0→3 instead of 0→6. The admin-share Fact builds its own tree with no cloud bits, and the Theory's tree is a separate TempTree root, so they never meet. The spike's asked 5 under B confirms the share Fact's tree is not masked.
2. The Theory leaves Kept unasserted, while the share asserts assert Kept == 0. These do not contradict each other. Locally, Kept depends on CFA allowing the write-attributes open. On the share, Kept ≤ Asked == 0.
3. The kill sets do not overlap. A fails only the 3 rows and B fails only the admin-share Fact (spike 873/873). Each mutant therefore has its own witness, and neither assertion relies on the other gate.
4. The survey's mutant run once wrote into the worktree through a relative path. The mutant contract now requires a git-archive copy, absolute paths and a final `git diff --exit-code src` = 0.
5. #388 ('one Fact is an undercount'): the spike ran the full default suite with the Theory in LastAccessTests and broke no pin. LastAccessRuleCorpusTests pins LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests, which this slice does not touch.

**What no earlier stage recorded.** No stage ran the acceptance repro's regex reader against the edited tree; the spikes ran only the default suite. The risk-spike stage should have, in its both-assertions experiment. Build must run it (case 14).

**Command name.** The survey's recorded acceptance command names `SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions.csproj`, but the engine ran `.Tests.csproj`. The engine's name is used here.

**architecture_rules is left empty on purpose.** This slice touches only test code and settles no dependency direction. The one convention it does set, literal Theory rows rather than rows derived from the mask, is already guarded by the single-bit mutant evidence. A fitness entry for it would add a settled rule. That shifts the RuleCases C-001/C-003 expected counts and needs a harness.py --scenario all run (#212, #273), a cost out of proportion to a one-file convention.

**No workaround applies**, so no KnownWorkarounds entry is added.

outside_claims.source: Investigation: a local handle gets error 87; known issue libmdbx#374 checked and not matched on 26200

outside_claims.if_wrong: Two more rows could be added. The design itself is unaffected.

outside_claims.claim: Opening an offline file and querying it by handle does not trigger a recall; only reading, writing or mapping it does.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Marking a temp folder OFFLINE could start recall machinery. There is no HSM behind the temp tree, so the practical risk is nil.

outside_claims.claim: xUnit reports each [InlineData] row of a [Theory] as its own test, so one failing bit names its row.
outside_claims.source: memory; consistent with the spike's trx, which listed rows Offline, 524288 and 1048576 separately
outside_claims.if_wrong: Per-bit failures would not be told apart. The kills would still happen.

prior_art.pattern: Cloud-placeholder masks go wrong through a missing or mislabelled bit (RECALL_ON_OPEN was absent; RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS was labelled 'Pinned'). Testing one row per flag guards against exactly that.
On-demand cloud locality is classified from the same attribute set the scanner masks (OFFLINE / PINNED / UNPINNED / RECALL_ON_*), without reading file contents.
Opening an offline file and querying it by handle does not recall it; only reading, writing or mapping does.

The constants OFFLINE 0x1000, RECALL_ON_OPEN 0x40000 and RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS 0x400000 match Kernel32.cs:29-33. PINNED and UNPINNED are absent from that table, which is why the Theory rows use hex literals with a name comment.
Mutation testing: judge a suite by the named mutants it kills, and check each mutant is non-equivalent before demanding a kill.
One [InlineData] row per enum flag in an xUnit [Theory], so each failure names its flag.

cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Each guard branch gets a named one-line mutant and a test that kills it. The acceptance evidence that an assertion bites is the mutant run in a scratch copy, not the green unmutated run. The discipline is used without a runner: the mutants are applied by hand once, in a scratch copy.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The defect is literally 'a surviving mutant': A and B each keep 870/870 green. Survey criteria (a') and (b') are mutant-kill criteria. The transfer also brings the classic traps in view: equivalent mutants, kills that happen only in an opt-in run, and test oracles derived from the code under test.

invariants.precondition: Each mutant is non-equivalent: removing the gate changes observable behaviour.
invariants.evidence: Investigation probe: mutant A takes la-tree local asked from 3 to 6. Mutant B takes b-tree through both admin shares from 0 to 4 asked, with 4 kept.

invariants.precondition: The killing test runs where standing protection is wanted, the default suite, not only in an opt-in run.
invariants.evidence: Spike both-assertions-turn-whole-suite-red-under-each-mutant: 873/873 unmutated; A fails 3 rows, B fails 1 admin-share Fact, under both TEMPs.

invariants.precondition: The test environment reaches the guarded branch: the admin share answers, reports NTFS, and FileRemoteProtocolInfo succeeds on it.
invariants.evidence: Holds on this PC (shareHosts = 2, fs NTFS, protocol 0x00020000). On a PC with admin shares off, the kill goes vacuous. Never measured elsewhere, nor on Windows 10 (Q-224).

invariants.precondition: Expected values are independent of the code under test: the rows are not derived from the mask.
invariants.evidence: Literal InlineData values. In the spike, each single-bit mutant failed only its own row.

invariants.precondition: Mutant runs never contaminate the real worktree.
invariants.evidence: The survey's first run wrote mutant B into the worktree's Scanner.cs through a relative path; it was reverted. Build uses a git-archive copy with absolute paths and ends with `git diff --exit-code src` = 0.

channeled_experts: Mutation-testing practitioners (PIT / Stryker): a surviving mutant is the bug, and its kill is the proof
Raymond Chen (The Old New Thing): what an offline file tolerates without a recall
xUnit maintainers: one Theory row per flag, so each failure names its bit
